# Instructions for Working on sitecore.ai.sdlc

This repo is the central source of AI instructions, agents, and MCP configs synced to downstream repositories. See `README.md` for full context on the system design.

## File Organization

| Path | Purpose | Synced? |
|------|---------|---------|
| `instructions/` | Behavioral guidance for AI | Yes → `.github/instructions/org/` |
| `agents/` | Custom Copilot agents | Yes → `.github/agents/` |
| `mcp/` | MCP server configs (Jira, Confluence) | Yes → `.vscode/mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json` |
| `service-context/` | Aggregated service contexts from all repos | No (reference only) |
| `sync/` | Sync scripts, repo lists (GitHub + ADO), test tooling | No |

## Rules for Instruction Files

- Place in `instructions/` with `.instructions.md` extension
- Include `owner` in frontmatter (GitHub team handle)
- One concern per file
- Use `applyTo` glob if it only applies to certain file types

## Rules for Agent Files

- Place in `agents/` with `.agent.md` extension
- Each agent should have a clear, focused purpose

## Rules for the Sync System

- Test changes with `--dry-run` first (both via workflow dispatch and `test-local.sh`)
- `sync/sync-one-repo.sh` handles one repo at a time — platform-aware (GitHub or ADO)
- `sync/sync-files.sh` runs in the context of each target repo — platform-agnostic, no GitHub or ADO API calls
- `CENTRAL_REPO_PATH` env var points to this repo's checkout
- Changes to `sync/` don't trigger auto-sync (only content folders do, plus repo list files)
- GitHub repos are enrolled in `sync/repos.txt` (format: `org/repo`)
- ADO repos are enrolled in `sync/ado-repos.txt` (format: `org/project/repo`)
- Orgs are discovered dynamically from both repo lists — never hardcode org names in workflows
- GitHub repos use GitHub App authentication (`APP_ID`, `APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets)
- ADO repos use Entra ID App Registrations with OIDC federation — per-org variables `ADO_SP_CLIENT_ID_{ORG}` and `ADO_SP_TENANT_ID_{ORG}` (no secrets needed)
- Each {org, platform} combination runs as a separate matrix job for parallelism

## Rules for Service Context Aggregation

- The aggregate workflow creates a PR (never pushes directly — branch is protected)
- Each service context has a `service:` field in frontmatter — names must be unique
- If two repos claim the same service name, aggregation fails loudly
- `service-context/` is reference only — it is NOT synced to downstream repos

## Things to Preserve

- The sync script seeds `.github/service-context.md`, `specs/`, `specs/archive/`, and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` in downstream repos only if they don't already exist — never overwrite team content
- `service-context/_index.md` is auto-generated by the aggregate workflow — don't edit manually
